Apple Log engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Apple Log rollout covers storefront language. Xcode, system frameworks, and Connect actually separate in-app log capture from product-page copy:

  • Camera Apple Log recording & profile picker UI — Apple Camera feature that records video in Apple Log color profile on supported iPhone models, with a flat log curve preview and log gamma encoding for post-production grading. Controls in-device capture behavior — not App Store language.
  • AVFoundation & log capture pipelines — frameworks some apps use to record or export log footage before or after capture. Your listing may mention Log profile or color grade handoff; building capture and encoder pipelines is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Color grading & NLE handoff — separate in-app or post-capture surfaces where log footage may export for grading in an NLE. Listing copy explains grading latitude and color grade benefits; LUT production and encoder wiring are outside AppLocale scope.
  • Camera permissions & capture entitlements — NSCameraUsageDescription, microphone access, and storage access when recording log video. Entitlements and capture wiring are platform work — distinct from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Apple Log to buyers.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Apple Log support in the binary.

A working Apple Log capture story and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.
